title: [v0.4.29] Epic: support host platforms
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Current release assignment and acceptance boundary

**Parent: #876 / v0.4.29; milestone v0.4.x.** #872 supplies the foundation; #174 is final v0.4.31 acceptance. Linux and real WSL2 require developer local/remote evidence. macOS arm64 requires Dev Local acceptance on **both Docker Desktop and Podman Machine**; macOS amd64 build/conformance is not runtime support without its own runtime evidence. macOS Dev Remote and automatic Keychain trust are explicitly deferred to #886; signing/notarization to #885. #882 is the separate Darwin build prerequisite, #883 the Podman Machine realization, #884 actual macOS runtime qualification.

This paragraph and #876 supersede older single-runtime, macOS-remote and v0.4.25 assignments below. Preserve the minimal Host seam and actual VM capacity/isolation evidence; unsupported/unqualified paths must not be advertised as supported.

---

## Goal

Define one small **Host Platform Contract** so BaseHarbor can reason about the machine/client platform without scattering Linux/Windows/macOS branches through Core, CLI, Runtime Providers or lifecycle code.

This is an independent architecture/portability track. It is not tied to a single release until explicitly scheduled.

Product rule:

```text
BaseHarbor semantics
        ↓
Host Platform Contract
        ↓
Linux | Windows/WSL2 | macOS
```

The contract must model only host/platform concerns that BaseHarbor genuinely needs. It must not become another general plugin framework.

## Why

Current code contains real host assumptions:

- `internal/hostresource/memory.go` reads Linux `/proc/meminfo` and PSI from `/proc/pressure/memory`.
- application memory preflight currently tells the user to verify `/proc/meminfo`.
- guided backup/restore uses `/proc/self/fd/<fd>` for an in-memory password-file path.
- `internal/hosttrust` automatically installs trust only on Linux and otherwise requires manual export.
- `baha update` currently packages/self-updates Linux amd64/arm64 only.
- Podman Quadlet realization assumes Linux `systemd --user` / `systemctl`; that is a Runtime Provider realization concern and must not leak into generic host semantics.
- runtime discovery commonly uses executable lookup, which is portable in principle but still needs platform-aware capability classification.
- browser opening already has explicit Darwin/Windows branches, proving some host-specific behavior already exists.
- XDG/home/path/state assumptions need review for Windows/macOS.
- Docker Desktop / Podman Machine / WSL2 mean **physical host capacity != effective runtime capacity**.

## Architectural boundary

The contract should be intentionally small. Candidate semantic capabilities:

```text
HostPlatform
├── Identity / classification
├── Effective resource evidence
├── Runtime discovery context
├── Trust-store operations
├── Filesystem/path semantics
├── Secure ephemeral-file/descriptor semantics
├── Browser/desktop handoff
├── Terminal/PTY capability
└── Service/lifecycle capability classification
```

Do not freeze these exact method names. First classify real callers, then define the minimum contract.

### Hard rules

- portable Application Intent MUST NOT contain host OS fields;
- Runtime Provider and Host Platform are separate axes;
- Target Access Provider and Host Platform are separate axes;
- no `if GOOS == ...` branches spread through domain/lifecycle code;
- Linux-specific runtime mechanics such as Quadlet/systemd stay inside the Podman Linux realization;
- physical host resource values must not be used when workloads actually run inside WSL2, Docker Desktop or Podman Machine with a smaller effective allocation;
- unsupported host capabilities fail explicitly with typed actionable diagnostics;
- no support claim without matching evidence.

## Platform scope

### Linux

Linux remains the reference host and must be migrated behind the contract without behavior regression.

### Windows

**v0.4 Windows strategy: Linux baha inside real WSL2 only. No native Windows executable/host adapter or Windows-container support is required or claimed.** Windows-runner build/conformance is supplementary evidence only and does not change this support boundary.

Distinguish:

```text
Windows native client host
!=
WSL2 Linux execution environment
```

WSL2 may use Linux semantics inside the VM, but effective runtime resources and trust/runtime boundaries must be classified correctly. Native Windows support must not be accidentally claimed merely because code compiles.

### macOS

Native Darwin `baha` should be able to use platform-native host operations while Docker Desktop / Podman Machine remain VM-backed runtimes. Effective runtime resources must come from the runtime VM/allocation where required, not from total physical Mac memory.

## Support/evidence vocabulary

Use explicit support levels, for example:

```text
SUPPORTED
TESTED
PORTABILITY-VERIFIED
EXPERIMENTAL
UNSUPPORTED
```

Exact terminology may align with the existing platform-support classification, but architecture conformance alone must never imply full runtime support.

## Testing strategy

### Shared conformance

- contract/unit tests with deterministic fake host implementations;
- platform capability/error semantics;
- resource evidence classification;
- path/filesystem behavior;
- trust operation/result semantics;
- secure temporary/ephemeral secret handling;
- no-dead-end diagnostics;
- architecture guard preventing direct platform-specific calls outside allowed adapters.

### Linux

- existing Linux CI and Docker/Podman acceptance remain authoritative;
- prove no regression after routing host operations through the contract.

### Windows / WSL2

- Windows GitHub-hosted runner for native build/unit/conformance where applicable;
- explicit WSL2 acceptance requires a runner/environment that genuinely provides WSL2; do not fake this with GOOS cross-compilation;
- real runtime smoke tests only where Docker/Podman/WSL2 are actually available.

### macOS

- GitHub-hosted macOS ARM64 and Intel runners for native build/unit/conformance;
- test filesystem/process/browser/trust adapter behavior that the runner can genuinely exercise;
- Docker Desktop / Podman Machine full lifecycle support requires real runtime evidence and is not implied by a native macOS test pass.

## Current code audit: initial hotspots

Known areas to inventory/refactor:

- `internal/hostresource/`
- `cmd/baha/app_memory_preflight.go`
- `cmd/baha/app_backup_restore_guided.go`
- `internal/hosttrust/`
- `internal/operatorauth/login.go`
- `internal/health/doctor.go`
- `cmd/baha/update.go`
- `internal/runtime/stack.go`
- `internal/deployment/target.go`
- `internal/orgconfig/store.go`
- `cmd/baha/path_prompt_linux.go`
- Podman Quadlet/systemd implementation under `internal/providers/runtime/podman/`

This list is a starting point, not a claim that every item belongs directly in the contract.

## Non-goals

- no generic OS plugin ecosystem;
- no requirement that every Runtime Provider work on every host;
- no claim of native Windows container support;
- no claim of full macOS Docker Desktop/Podman Machine support without runtime evidence;
- no moving Podman Quadlet/systemd mechanics into the Host Platform Contract;
- no Application Contract changes solely for host portability.

## Acceptance

- [ ] real host-dependent call sites are inventoried and classified;
- [ ] minimal Host Platform Contract is documented and implemented;
- [ ] Linux behavior is routed through the contract with no regression;
- [ ] Windows native vs WSL2 semantics are explicit;
- [ ] macOS native host semantics are explicit;
- [ ] effective runtime capacity is distinguished from physical host capacity;
- [ ] trust/filesystem/secure-ephemeral/browser/terminal semantics have explicit capability behavior;
- [ ] unsupported capabilities fail closed with actionable next steps;
- [ ] architecture guard prevents new unapproved host-specific branching outside adapters;
- [ ] shared conformance suite exists;
- [ ] CI matrix records what is actually tested per platform;
- [ ] platform support documentation matches evidence and does not overclaim;
- [ ] no portable Application Intent or provider contract needs host-specific fields.


## Child issues / implementation order

- [ ] #819 — inventory, minimal interface and architecture guard
- [ ] #820 — Linux reference adapter and regression acceptance
- [ ] #821 — WSL2 host behavior and explicit native-Windows exclusions
- [ ] #822 — macOS Darwin adapter and CI qualification
- [ ] #823 — cross-platform conformance, CI matrix and support evidence

Recommended order:

```text
#819 contract/inventory
  ↓
#820 Linux migration proves no regression
  ↓
#821 Windows/WSL2   ||   #822 macOS
  ↓
#823 shared conformance/support evidence
```

#821 and #822 can proceed in parallel once #819 stabilizes the seam.

## Evidence rule

A platform may land at a different support level without blocking the contract:

```text
Linux       -> SUPPORTED when current real runtime gates remain green
Windows     -> native client/adapter support outside v0.4; Windows-runner checks alone confer no support
WSL2        -> TESTED/SUPPORTED only after real WSL2 execution evidence
macOS       -> PORTABILITY-VERIFIED from real Darwin CI; full runtime support only after Docker Desktop/Podman Machine E2E evidence
```

The architecture work is successful if later platform qualification can improve these levels without changing BaseHarbor portable application semantics.


## Historical, superseded assignment — v0.4.25 (2026-10-09)

**Parent release:** #174. This is now a blocking v0.4.25 implementation umbrella, not an unscheduled architecture-only track. Child order remains #819 -> #820 -> (#821 || #822) -> #823. Architecture audit #817 is a companion acceptance slice.

**Definition of done** requires the real developer workflow on macOS native (Darwin arm64/amd64) and on an actual Windows WSL2 Linux environment with a validated Linux-container runtime configuration. Install/update, path/trust/credentials, Core/Target selection, application init/plan/up/status/doctor, SQL/cache access, logs and owned destroy must work with documented boundaries. Dev Remote enrollment/import and mTLS must be proven. Runtime VM resource constraints must be measured accurately. Record exact-head native/WSL and disposable runtime tests before declaring supported.

**Scope prioritization:** First support one reliable Docker Desktop or Podman Machine path on macOS and one reliable WSL2 Docker or Podman path; expand verified configurations as evidence permits. Native Windows binary/container support is not required for the WSL2 acceptance, and systemd-only Podman Quadlet must not be misrepresented as working natively on macOS. Do not mark this parent done based only on mocked adapters, cross-builds or architecture guards.


---

## Release assignment (2026-10-10)
This platform item now belongs to **v0.4.29 #876**, not the old v0.4.25 plan. Two sessions: Host/Linux/WSL2 (#819–#821) and Darwin/macOS + qualification (#822–#823); final audit #817. Host contract semantics must be pinned in v0.4.25 #872 and consumed here without silent redefinition; final release-wide acceptance #174 is v0.4.31. Real runtime evidence required.

comments.body:
## macOS supplement (2026-10-14) — additional child issues

The binding macOS target and decisions D1–D5 are recorded in #876 ("macOS supplement"); #817, #819, #820, #822 and #823 carry matching supplements.

**Additional children for v0.4.29:**

- [ ] #882 — restore darwin compilation + darwin build/vet CI gate (**pulled ahead**, target `develop`)
- [ ] #883 — Podman Machine: existing Quadlet realization executed inside the machine VM (provider-internal executor seam)
- [ ] #884 — self-hosted Apple Silicon runner for real Docker Desktop / Podman Machine evidence

**Follow-ups (not v0.4.29):**

- #885 — Developer ID signing and notarization of darwin artifacts
- #886 — automatic Keychain trust and Dev Remote on macOS (deferred from #822)

**Updated order:**

```text
#882 (ahead) → #819 (+ D1/D2 contract review) → #820
  → (#821 WSL2 || #822 macOS + #883 Podman Machine)
  → #823 (+ #884 runtime lane) → #817 audit
```

**Notes on this issue's text:**

- *Scope prioritization* ("one reliable Docker Desktop **or** Podman Machine path") is extended for macOS to **both** Docker Desktop and Podman Machine on darwin/arm64.
- *Effective resource evidence* in the candidate list moves to the runtime engine observation (D2, see #819) and is no longer a Host Platform capability.
- Hosted macOS runners provide native build/unit/conformance only. Runtime E2E evidence comes from #884, because hosted Apple Silicon runners have no nested virtualization.
- Dev Remote on macOS moves from the definition of done to #886. WSL2 Dev Remote is unchanged.
